opening_message:
Ticket 1: Erika Bolton (employee ID E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 6 note(s) about employee E002.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Erika Bolton (E002) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. Full-time employees max out at write, and admin requires the employee's role to own the system. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, not Analyst, so the maximum allowed is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by IT agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Erika Bolton (E002) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, not Analyst, so admin is not permitted for full-time employees. Maximum allowed is write; requested admin exceeds max, so recommend granting write.
Note 3 (ticket 1), written by Finance agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Finance record confirms E002 (Erika Bolton) is a full-time Analyst. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, not Analyst, so admin is not permitted for full-time employees. Maximum allowed is write; requested admin exceeds max. Recommend granting write.
Note 4 (ticket 1), written by Compliance agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Compliance confirms E002 (Erika Bolton) is a full-time Analyst. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, not Analyst, so admin is not permitted for full-time employees. Maximum allowed is write; requested admin exceeds max. Recommend granting write.
Note 5 (ticket 1), written by Facilities agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Facilities record confirms E002 (Erika Bolton) is an Analyst. As a full-time Analyst requesting admin to Payroll: Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, not Analyst, so admin is not permitted for full-time employees. Maximum allowed is write; requested admin exceeds max. Recommend granting write.
Note 6 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB record for E002 (Erika Bolton) shows contractor with basic security training. Despite other notes listing full-time, the Security record is authoritative: contractors max out at read (write requires advanced training; admin never allowed). Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Erika Bolton (E002) requested admin access to Payroll. Five of six notes (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) consistently identify E002 as a full-time Analyst. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, not Analyst, so the full-time employee's maximum is write (admin requires the employee's role to own the system). Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so the maximum of write is granted. The single Security note claims contractor status, but this contradicts the weight of corroborating records, so full-time treatment applies.

content.text:
Let me work through this. The ticket: Erika Bolton requests admin access to Payroll.

Notes: HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities all say full-time Analyst, recommend write (max for full-time non-owner is write; requested admin exceeds max, grant write).

Security note says the Security DB record shows contractor with basic security training, recommends read.

There's a conflict: employment type full_time vs contractor. The Security agent claims its record is authoritative, but that's an assertion. In this environment, the team notes reflect facts. The majority of agents (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) confirm full-time Analyst. Security claims contractor.

Which is authoritative? Typically HR is authoritative for employment type. Actually, the policy mentions contractors with advanced security training can get write. Security tracks training. But the employment type discrepancy matters.

Hmm, how do we resolve conflicting facts? We need to make a decision. The majority (5 notes) say full-time. One (Security) says contractor. The Security note itself says "Despite other notes listing full-time, the Security record is authoritative" - but that's just Security's claim.

As Approver, I should weigh the information. Most sources agree Erika is a full-time Analyst. The recommended level by those agents is write. Requested admin exceeds write max, so grant write.

Alternatively, if contractor with basic training, max read.

Which to choose? I think the majority evidence supports full-time. The security agent's claim of contractor isn't corroborated by any other source; 5 sources agree full-time. I'll go with write.

Let me submit write with reasoning.
